newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Japan asks Bangladesh to develop infrastructure.
newsitem.headline: Japan asks Bangladesh to develop infrastructure.

text.p: Bangladesh, desperately trying to woo foreign investment, needs to develop infrastructure, ensure political stability and make quick decisions, a Japanese business leader said on Saturday.

"It will be difficult for the Japanese investors to come if there is no smooth power supply in the country," Uzuhiko Uwatoko, Chairman of Japan-Bangladesh Committee for Commercial and Economic Cooperation, told Reuters.
He said Japanese investors were studying the prospect of investment in Bangladesh.
"I am trying hard that there is increased Japanese investment in Bangladesh," he said.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, opening the committee's eighth meeting on Saturday, assured Japanese entrepreneurs that her government would ensure adequate supply of power, tele-links and other infrastructural facilities.
"Bangladesh has many prospective areas to attract Japanese investment and we offer an extensive and fabulous package of incentives and facilities," she said.
Hasina said Bangladesh needed to raise investment to 25 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) from the present 15-16 percent to spur economic growth to sevent percent from 5.0 percent at present.

Bangladesh offers foreign investors a tax holiday of up to 12 years, allows repatriation of capital, profit and dividend, waives duty on imported capital machinery for 100 percent export-oriented industries and exempts income tax up to three years for foreign technicians.
Yussuf Abdullah Haroon, President of the Federation of Bangladesh Chamber of Commerce and Industry, said Japan had already invested $247 million in 13 projects in Chittagong Export Processing Zone.
